findings.text: blocking: the runs pre-flight judges source/scope by raw membership (`if source not in RUN_SOURCES` / `if scope not in RUN_SCOPES`), while the view that owns the check normalizes first (reckon/crew/query.py:802 `str(source or "all").strip().lower()`), so mcp._crew(project='fixture', view='runs', source='ALL') is refused with 'runs source must be one of all, ledger, live' and the same call with scope='Project' with "unknown runs scope 'Project'"; both were served before this change and are still served through serve_crew_view, so the pre-flight refuses a well-formed request - the inversion reckon/mcp.py:295-303's own docstring forbids.

non-blocking: the runs source/scope validation is restated in the pre-flight rather than delegated to reckon/crew/query.py:802-810, which owns it, and the restatement is what let the two diverge in normalization and in wording ('runs source must be one of ...' here against 'unknown runs scope ...; scope must be one of ...' there); extracting the owner's check as a no-I/O validator, as crew_view_name and normalize_roadmap_view were extracted in this same node, would hold both surfaces to one fact.
